figures.sourceContext: Section 11.3 Example 7 describes stereographic projection from the omitted pole P to the tangent plane at its antipode, contracting a based loop in the punctured sphere. The sphere itself is not contractible, though its fundamental group is trivial.
facts: Sphere/PuncturedSphere, SpherePunctureOf, SphereLoopAvoids, SphereLoopContractionOf, LoopBasedAt, NullHomotopic and NotContractible distinguish loop contraction from contraction of the entire sphere. P is outside the loop image and y0 is the base point.
limits: The source figure is a schematic fan of loop slices, not a faithful orthographic projection of the exact stereographic homotopy. Native curves share the fixed base point and are clipped to the sphere silhouette; helpers separately evaluate the actual based homotopy.

The source shortcut assumes a pole outside a loop image. The concrete program asserts this hypothesis and does not claim every arbitrary continuous loop has a proper image; a space-filling loop need not admit that shortcut. The established triviality of the sphere fundamental group is recorded separately.
Figure 11.18 is on missing printed page248; the supplied stereographic prose is used, but that missing figure is not reconstructed.

figures.sourceContext: Section 11.3 Example 8 applies the product fundamental-group theorem to C×C, obtaining Z direct-sum Z with the two factor loops a,b representing its two generators.
facts: Both TorusFactorLoop entities have unit winding in distinct factors and share a ProductPoint y0. Loop classes belong to the fundamental group, which is isomorphic to the binary direct sum and the rank-two free abelian group.
limits: The native torus is the source-like flattened schematic, with ellipse silhouette/hole and widened meridian, rather than a metrically faithful projected mesh. Source solid/dashed traversal conventions and arrows are retained.
torusFactorPoint separately samples exact loops in the product of circles; source display geometry does not redefine the product or its loops.
The marked base point is independently verified on both native generator curves.

figures.sourceContext: Section 11.3 Exercise5 changes base point along an arc j from y1 to y0; the isomorphism sends |a| to |j#a#j^-1|.
facts: j and its reverse are TopologicalPath entities with reversed endpoints; a is a loop at y0 and its conjugate a loop at y1. BasepointChangeAlong and GroupIsomorphismBetween encode the transport.
limits: The two near-parallel traces show opposite traversals of the same arc image, rather than two separate mathematical edges. ReversedPathOf is used because j is not itself a based loop.
Source bounds stop before the caption; the render canvas retains one extra vertical pixel for label padding.
Smooth native contour approximates the hand-drawn loop while preserving labels a,y0,y1,j,j^-1 and arrow directions.

figures.sourceContext: Section 11.4 Definition5 and Example10: a contractible X has the same homotopy type as singleton Y={P}, using f(x)=P and g(P)=x0.
facts: ConstantTo(f,P), MapsTo(g,P,x0), CompositionOf(k,g,f), CompositionOf(iY,f,g), HomotopyBetween(H,iX,k), HomotopyInverseMaps and HomotopyEquivalent retain the correct map domains.
limits: The source prints the X/Y composite names in the opposite order: f∘g=k~iX and g∘f=iY. This is type-inconsistent for the stated f:X→Y and g:Y→X. Substance uses the correctly typed g∘f=k~iX and f∘g=iY; no corrected equations are introduced into the picture.
The generic contractible contour belongs to Style; its source hatches, x0 dot, original knockout, singleton dot and f/g arrows remain, with subdued orange fill.

figures.sourceContext: Section 11.4 Exercise2 asks to classify eleven planar diagram spaces by homotopy type: A,B,C,D,E,R,T, the animal, the house, 8 and the connected compound 108.
facts: PlanarDiagramSpace and FiniteGraphSpine are reusable coarse descriptors. The representative spines have one vertex and ranks A1,B2,C0,D1,E0,R1,T0,animal2,house2,82,1083. Their fundamental groups are modeled by corresponding free groups.
limits: Bold native vector contours approximate the source typeface; even-odd interior contours preserve transparent holes independently of host fonts. No answers or extra labels are shown in the source reproduction.
The compound 108 has touching source ink. Two native joins preserve that connected space with three holes; rendering three isolated text characters would alter its homotopy type.

The house chimney encloses a second cycle, while the animal has closed head/body loops and attached tree legs/tail. Graph spines describe the printed planar geometry rather than arbitrary drawings of those objects.
Classification facts concern these explicit vector spaces; a differently drawn glyph or disconnected typography may have a different homotopy type.
